summary.headline: Aarti Industries Q2 FY27 revenue rose 73% YoY to Rs 3,887 crore and EBITDA hit a record Rs 418 crore (+44% YoY), helped by raw-material pass-through.
summary.overview: Aarti Industries reported record quarterly revenue and EBITDA for Q2 FY27, with H1 EBITDA above Rs 802 crore against Rs 507 crore a year earlier. Growth was driven by volumes and by passing through higher raw-material costs, with Energy-linked products the main contributor. Net debt rose above Rs 4,650 crore on working capital and finance costs, prompting a Rs 1,000 crore fund-raise enabling resolution approved by shareholders on 31 October 2026. Zone IV Phase I was commissioned on 7 September 2026, with most of the Rs 1,800-1,900 crore CWIP expected to be capitalised by 31 March 2027.

segments.name: Energy-linked portfolio (Fuel Additives/MMA, Calcium Chloride)
segments.commentary: Revenue roughly doubled sequentially from about Rs 1,000 crore to about Rs 1,900 crore, per analyst; supported by strong gasoline-naphtha cracks and price pass-through. Fuel Additives capacity expanded from 290 KTPA to 360 KTPA in Q1 2026, and management says spreads were maintained, not expanded. Energy now close to 50% of revenue; mid-term target is 30-40% of portfolio.

segments.name: Dyes & Pigments (NCB chain)
segments.commentary: Steady growth on resilient domestic demand; NCB utilisation elevated and expansion (debottlenecking rather than greenfield) under evaluation. Spreads expanded versus original assumption.

segments.name: Agrochemicals (AgChem)
segments.commentary: Volume growth in select categories, pricing mixed. Quarterly contracts cause a one-quarter lag in pass-through; H2 may reflect weaker domestic monsoon.

segments.name: Pharma & Fluoro (PNCB, paracetamol building blocks)
segments.commentary: Pricing and volume gains in PNCB, aided by Chinese capacity rationalisation. Fluoro margins remain under pressure.

segments.name: Polymers & Additives (PDA, DCB)
segments.commentary: PDA softness was a short-term drag on Q2; PDA capacity is being re-evaluated amid Chinese overcapacity and dumping. DCB capacity debottlenecked to 140 KTPA and expected to pick up in H2 on US flows.

segments.name: Acid value chain
segments.commentary: Sulphur price rose 5-6x; pass-through was difficult and margins compressed significantly.

guidance_outlook: Management did not revise the Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance; said momentum should continue, but H2 may soften in winter. Fresh FY28 guidance to come closer to year-end.
FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800-2,200 crore referenced by an analyst; management said it remains on track across cost, volume/margin and capex levers.
Zone IV: targets Rs 250-350 crore bottom line over the first 18 months and aims for EBITDA-accretive operation in FY28; 5-10 products in FY27, 20-25 products across 5 chemistry blocks by FY28.
FY27 capex planned at Rs 700-800 crore; new capacity focus is debottlenecking and brownfield rather than greenfield.
Tax rate guided at 15-20% for FY27/FY28, with deferred tax liabilities rising as new assets commercialise.
Augene Chemicals JV (with Superform): commercial production expected soon, steady-state revenue Rs 300-400 crore.
New 10+ year supply agreement signed 13 October 2026 with a global specialty chemical major: revenue potential about Rs 1,500 crore, capex under US$25 million, commercial operations targeted FY29.
capex_capacity: Zone IV Phase I (Jhagadia) commissioned 7 September 2026: Calcium Chloride unit, PEDA plant and part of the Multipurpose Plant are operational and stabilising; Calcium Chloride exceeded design capacity within three months, PEDA reached design norms within two months.
CWIP of about Rs 2,200 crore at September 2026, of which Rs 1,800-1,900 crore (mostly Zone IV) expected to be capitalised by 31 March 2027.
Fuel Additives capacity 360 KTPA (up from 290 KTPA); MMA ran almost at full capacity in Q2.
DCB debottlenecked to 140 KTPA, aligned with downstream PDCB demand; NCB expansion under evaluation on customer requests.
Rs 1,000 crore fund-raise enabling resolution approved by shareholders in EGM on 31 October 2026, aimed at deleveraging.
demand_pricing: Non-energy demand described as steady and strong; NCB demand very strong, DCB H2-weighted on US flows.
Raw material costs rose sharply on Middle East tensions; Sulphur up 5-6x. Methanol supply is available but volatile in price; Aniline supply from China is constrained and Europe supply is starting.
Gasoline-naphtha cracks were above USD 20 per barrel in the prior quarter; Q2 energy spreads were maintained rather than expanded.
Chinese anti-involution policy and removal of VAT rebates (up to 13% of product price) cited as a lever that could lift NCB and potentially PDA spreads.
Management says PDA faces Chinese overcapacity and dumping; plant may be partly redirected to other products.
Long-term contracts represent about 25-30% of business; fixed costs and conversion margins largely protected in these contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be stronger than H1 and should FY27 EBITDA exceed the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was unusual due to energy pull-up; H2 momentum expected to continue but may soften in winter. Risks include Zone IV fixed costs from Q4 and a sharp crude correction affecting inventory. Guidance update deferred to year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Zone IV CWIP will be capitalised and what is the revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 1,800-1,900 crore to be capitalised by 31 March 2027. Management declined to give a revenue number, citing crude volatility; it targets Rs 250-350 crore bottom line over 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: How are the inflationary raw-material costs affecting margins and which segment is hurt?
qa_highlights.answer: Acid chain (sulphur) had incomplete pass-through and compressed margins. AgChem intermediates see a 3-4 month lag. About two-thirds of the portfolio held per-kg spreads; more than two-thirds operates on pass-through in absolute rupees. Rs 800-1,000 crore of inventory is on the water.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any trading volume in the top line?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, about Rs 500 crore of trading volume in H1, done to build market for expanded capacity; partly explains lower Q2 margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to expand MMA/energy capacity beyond 360 KTPA?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term priority is stabilising at 360 KTPA and building integrated value chain presence (raw-material arrangements, downstream integration). Further expansion to be evaluated later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-term contract share of business and what is the new contract's nature?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term partnerships are about 25-30% of business, with aspiration to increase. The new contract includes conversion-margin minimums plus process technology support and is the first such technology in India for this customer.

risks_watch: Crude and crack reversal could hit energy revenue and create inventory losses; forward booking used to mitigate but risk cannot be eliminated.
Zone IV ramp-up and fixed-cost absorption from Q4 FY27; commercial batch qualification still ongoing.
Rising net debt above Rs 4,650 crore and higher finance costs; Rs 1,000 crore raise pending execution.
Aniline supply constraints and dependence on China for MMA feedstock; methanol price tied to Middle East.
PDA chain overcapacity and Chinese dumping; no near-term volume growth planned.
Weaker monsoon could affect agrochemical demand in H2.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the long-term outlook, but cautious on near-term visibility: management repeatedly declined to give margin percentages, revenue potential for Zone IV, or FY28 guidance until year-end. Candid about pass-through lags and weak segments (PDA, fluoro, acid chain).
key_quotes: Aarti Industries has delivered its highest-ever quarterly and half yearly revenue and EBITDA, a testament to our strong operational performance and sustained business momentum.
The aspiration is to get Zone IV additive to EBITDA in FY28 itself and that is the current plan.
So there is no reason that we expect discontinuation of business performance from any of these contracts.

growth.why: Q2 revenue +73% and EBITDA +44% YoY with the Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance not revised and FY27 capex of Rs 700-800 crore held; growth backed by Zone IV Phase I commissioning, Fuel Additives expansion and a 10+ year supply agreement (~Rs 1,500 crore revenue potential, commercial ops FY29), though management flagged H2 softening and no explicit revenue growth guide was given.
